concerns.text: Task T015 (compute rsFC and Global Efficiency) lists a dependency on T014 (weighted adjacency) but incorrectly states it must run after T014. T014 produces binary/thresholded matrices AND the weighted matrix. T015 consumes the weighted matrix. However, T015 is marked [P] (parallel-safe) in the list, which is incorrect if it depends on T014's output file generation. If T014 is not complete, T015 cannot run. The [P] tag is misleading here as it implies independence from T014's completion.

Task T025 (compute z-scores for all three density thresholds) is marked [P] (parallel-safe) but explicitly depends on T014 (which generates the three binary adjacency files). T025 cannot run in parallel with T014. The [P] tag is a semantic violation of the 'Producer before consumer' rule.

Task T039 (aggregate metrics) depends on T027 (US2 output) and T015 (US1 output). T039 is not marked [P], which is correct, but the dependency chain is broken in the text: T015 is marked [P] (incorrectly, see above) and T027 is marked [X] (complete) while T025 (its producer) is marked [ ]. This creates a logical ordering violation where a consumer (T039) is listed as ready to run while its producer (T025) is incomplete.

Task T024 (timeout wrapper) is listed as a separate task after T022 (motif implementation). The Plan states the timeout wrapper is 'implemented' in the feasibility notes, but T022 is marked [X] (complete) while T024 is [ ]. This suggests the timeout logic is missing from the 'complete' T022, creating a hidden dependency where T022 is not actually complete without T024. T024 should be a prerequisite to T022 or merged into it.

Task T032 (permutation test) is marked [X] (complete) but depends on T030 (partial correlation) and T033 (zero-variance/VIF check), both of which are marked [ ] (pending/incomplete). A consumer task cannot be marked complete before its producers are complete. This violates the 'Producer before consumer' ordering principle.
